place the CT grid before the scout, or use the virtual grid. Select a path avoiding bowel, vessels, and pleura; mark the skin entry.
use sterile gloves/gown, skin prep, drapes, and towels. With lidocaine, syringe, and injection needle, raise a skin wheal and anesthetize the tract.
leave the anesthetic needle as a marker; check its angle on CT before exchanging it.

replace the marker with an 18G access needle/coaxial introducer; choose length for measured depth. Advance under CT guidance. Confirm the tip in fluid, remove the stylet, and aspirate into a specimen container for ordered studies.
advance a compatible 0.035-inch short Amplatz into the collection. Stop for resistance; confirm wire position on CT before removing the needle.

flush the MPD (commonly 10.2 Fr; alternatives 8.5, 12, 14 Fr) and insert its metal stiffener. Prepare the matched dilator. Measure needle depth from skin to collection and mark the planned dilator/drain depth.
hold the wire, remove the introducer, and make a scalpel skin nick. Advance the dilator over the wire to the marked depth; remove it without losing wire access.
advance drain/stiffener over the wire to the marked depth under CT. Tee off: hold the stiffener stationary and advance the drain off it. Keep the rigid tip within the collection.
remove wire and stiffener; form and lock the pigtail. Confirm the loop and all sideholes are inside the collection.
suture to skin without constricting the drain; connect the drainage bag and apply a dressing. Save a final CT for position and complications.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.

blocks.title: Access care
items: Flush with 10 mL sterile saline twice daily.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: 24 hours.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours.
DOACs: Typically 24 hours; confirm agent and renal function.
Clopidogrel: 75 mg dose - 6 hours; 300-600 mg loading dose - 24 hours.
Aspirin: 24 hours.
Restart after hemostasis is confirmed; individualize timing for procedure-specific or patient-specific exceptions.

blocks.title: Discharge - if outpatient
items: Discharge order with medication reconciliation - 30 minutes.
